current_p1: For one specified reduced or continuum vacuum-layer-jamming beam model under quasi-static planar bending, establish output-specific, predeclared model-form acceptance tolerances and independently validate tolerance-crossing validity and breakdown boundaries over vacuum pressure, layer count, and bending amplitude against an interface-resolving reference. The study must test whether vacuum-generated normal contact, Coulomb capacity, stick/partial-slip/gross-slip evolution, and contact redistribution invalidate assumptions such as zero gap, prescribed contact pressure, or friction that is not dominant; novelty cannot rest on frictional homogenization, discrete-contact benchmarking, a finite layer sweep, or an adopted percentage-error boundary alone.
executive_summary: C03 does not satisfy the complete kill condition, but it substantially narrows P1. Wang et al. (2026), paper_id ca46dc062d, already provide the closest framework: a named continuum theory for multilayer structures, homogenized Coulomb friction driven by contact stress, a penalty-based discrete-contact reference, layer-count and deformation sweeps, quantitative displacement errors, an explicit 5% applicability threshold, resulting rotation limits, and experimental comparison for 35-, 50-, and 70-layer bending stacks. Therefore, frictional multilayer homogenization, continuum-versus-discrete error mapping, and even a declared percentage-based applicability boundary are not sufficient novelty. Flexible-pipe studies additionally connect pressure and initial contact stress to Coulomb capacity, stick-transition-slip bending, full-layer references, reduced helix-contact models, and experiments. Rough-contact, equivalent-thin-layer, Iwan, steel-polymer, and soft-hard-joint studies supply pressure/preload-dependent friction and experimentally supported slip evolution. The remaining kill components are nevertheless absent: no supplied framework experimentally validates the tolerance-crossing breakdown boundary itself, and no framework demonstrates transfer from vacuum pressure to spatially evolving layer contact without additional contact mechanics. The closest continuum model assumes negligible interlayer gaps, warns that large friction violates its Kirchhoff-Love basis, and does not sweep vacuum-driven pressure. The flexible-pipe reduced model shows that assuming constant contact pressure causes error, but supplies no predeclared model-form tolerance boundary. Thus P1 survives only as a vacuum-specific, experimentally validated boundary problem, not as a generic continuum-model or friction-homogenization contribution.

paper_audits.title: The existence of a critical length scale in regularised friction
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Dynamic slip rupture along a two-dimensional deformable elastic half-space against a rigid flat surface.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Classical Coulomb friction regularized by a simplified Prakash-Clifton evolution law; interface opening is suppressed.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Regularized friction law whose small-characteristic-length limit approaches classical Coulomb behavior.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Normal contact stress enters the evolving regularized frictional strength; nucleation is imposed through a transient reduction of contact pressure.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Coulomb friction with equal static and kinetic coefficients, filtered through Prakash-Clifton regularization.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Dynamic rupture and slip propagation are studied; the paper does not construct a quasi-static multilayer stick/partial-slip/gross-slip beam model.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: A prescribed spatiotemporal pressure reduction nucleates slip, but evolving multilayer contact redistribution is not modeled.
paper_audits.reference_model: Mesh-refined explicit finite-element solutions and the classical-Coulomb limiting response.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: None; an experimental identification procedure is proposed.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Relative propagation-distance error below 0.5% and arrival-time error below 0.1% are used for mesh convergence; Lc=10^-5 m is reported for the analyzed system.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: A critical regularization length below which further reduction does not alter dynamic slip outputs, plus numerical mesh-error criteria.
paper_audits.declared_tolerance: 0.5% propagation-distance error and 0.1% arrival-time error, both numerical convergence tolerances rather than physical model-form acceptance tolerances.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Dynamic two-dimensional plane-strain sliding of a linear elastic half-space against a rigid plane in a well-posed, no-opening regime.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: The L-nd convergence map and critical regularization length delimit numerical and spectral influence, not reduced multilayer model breakdown.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: A friction regularization length and event frequency can control dynamic slip predictions and mesh requirements.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not establish quasi-static beam homogenization validity, a vacuum-pressure sweep, experiments, or a physical tolerance-defined continuum breakdown boundary.

paper_audits.title: Transition from stick to slip in Hertzian contact with “Griffith” friction: The Cattaneo–Mindlin problem revisited
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Quasi-static tangential loading of an elastically similar Hertzian spherical contact.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Hertz pressure combined with a Griffith mode-II slip-inception condition and Coulomb friction in the slip annulus.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Analytical Cattaneo-Mindlin-type contact model augmented by a fracture-energy stick-zone correction.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Normal load sets the Hertz pressure field and contact size; an optional pressure-dependent friction toughness changes the critical stick-zone scaling.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Coulomb sliding capacity in the slip annulus plus a Griffith fracture criterion at the stick-slip boundary.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Complete stick persists to a nonzero Qmin, partial slip follows, and global sliding occurs through unstable collapse at a critical stick-zone radius.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: The Hertz pressure distribution is explicit, but multilayer bending-induced redistribution is absent and elastic similarity decouples normal and tangential fields.
paper_audits.reference_model: Classical Cattaneo-Mindlin theory and analytical limiting comparisons.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: No new experiment; the paper discusses prior PMMA and oscillatory-contact observations.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: No reduced-versus-interface-resolving model-form error map is supplied.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Critical stick-zone size and associated Qmin/Qmax define physical slip transitions.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Quasi-static, axisymmetric, linear-elastic, elastically similar Hertzian contacts with no normal adhesion.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: The critical stick radius is a physical instability boundary, not a tolerance-defined reduced-model failure boundary.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: Normal loading and pressure-dependent toughness can govern stick, partial slip, and abrupt gross sliding.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not compare a multilayer continuum model with a discrete-layer reference or validate a model-form acceptance boundary for vacuum-jammed beams.

paper_audits.title: Friction Characteristics of CFRP Plates in Contact with Copper Plates under High Contact Pressure
paper_audits.physical_analogue: A unidirectional CFRP strip pulled between two copper clamping plates under high transverse pressure.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Nominally uniform double-sided contact with experimentally characterized friction and wear.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Empirical Amontons linear law for hard copper and Howell-type pressure power law for annealed copper.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Pressure directly changes shear capacity, friction coefficient for annealed copper, sliding distance, wear mechanism, and failure mode.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: For as-received copper, tau=0.31 sigma; for annealed copper, tau=1.02 sigma^0.76 with decreasing apparent friction coefficient.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Periodic stick-slip at 50–100 MPa is attributed to debris accumulation and release; high pressures produce ploughing and rupture.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Not resolved; normal stress is assumed uniform over the nominal contact areas.
paper_audits.reference_model: No interface-resolving or discrete-layer reference model.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Direct pullout experiments across six pressure levels and two copper conditions.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Regression fits are reported, including R²=0.97 and 0.92, but no reduced-model error against a reference.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Observed pressure regimes separate debris-mediated stick-slip from severe ploughing and premature rupture.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Dry CFRP-copper pullout at one displacement rate and 50–175 MPa nominal contact pressure.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Material rupture prevents characterization above 175 MPa; this is an experimental/material limit, not continuum-model breakdown.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: Friction capacity and damage mechanism can depend nonlinearly on contact pressure and counterface condition.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not provide a multilayer reduced model, discrete reference, model-form error map, or vacuum-pressure validity criterion.

paper_audits.title: A full layered numerical model for predicting hysteretic behavior of unbonded flexible pipes considering initial contact pressure
paper_audits.physical_analogue: A nine-layer unbonded flexible pipe under internal pressure and quasi-static cyclic cantilever bending.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Full-layer three-dimensional hard normal contact with penalty enforcement and Coulomb tangential friction between adjacent layers and armor tendons.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Equivalent orthotropic shells are used for selected carcass and pressure-armor layers, but the principal bending model is full layered rather than a reduced-versus-full validity study.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Internal pressure and manufacturing-induced sheath prestress determine interlayer contact forces, friction moment, curvature, and hysteresis.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Coulomb friction capacity under hard normal contact; calibrated coefficients vary with the tested pressure cases.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Tendon slip initiates near the neutral axis and progresses toward intrados and extrados through stick, transition, and slip phases.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Resolved by the full contact model; solid polymer layers change contact forces through Poisson effects.
paper_audits.reference_model: The full-layer 3D Abaqus contact model is the highest-fidelity model, but no distinct reduced model is systematically error-mapped against it here.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Full-scale cyclic bending data at three internal pressures are reproduced; the 2 MPa initial prestress and other uncertain geometry parameters are calibrated, so independent validation is not established.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Agreement with measured moment-curvature loops is reported, but no common scalar reduced-versus-full model-form error or tolerance map is supplied.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: No physical model-form acceptance criterion; friction coefficient above 0.2 affects solver choice and runtime.
paper_audits.validity_domain: One four-inch pipe geometry under 0.1 Hz cyclic bending, three internal pressures, room temperature, and no external effective tension.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: No tolerance-defined reduced-model breakdown boundary; transfer of the calibrated initial prestress to other pipes is explicitly unresolved.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: Pressure and initial contact stress can govern multilayer Coulomb stick-slip bending and experimental hysteresis in a full-layer structure.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not establish an accepted reduced model, predeclared model-form tolerance, or experimentally validated continuum breakdown map transferable to vacuum-jammed sheets.

paper_audits.title: Experimental validation of the applicability of effective spring boundary conditions for modelling damaged interfaces in laminate structures
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Three-layer aluminium-epoxy laminates with manufactured interfacial damage interrogated by ultrasonic guided waves.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Zero-thickness effective spring boundary conditions with equal normal and tangential stiffness and traction continuity.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Effective Spring Boundary Conditions derived from quasi-static micromechanical crack-density relations.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Curing pressure is reported, but operational pressure-dependent friction capacity is absent.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: No Coulomb friction or gross-slip capacity; displacement jump is linearly related to traction.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: None; static damaged adhesive interfaces are represented by springs.
paper_audits.reference_model: Micromechanical crack models and measured guided-wave dispersion; no frictional discrete-contact model.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Guided-wave measurements across pristine, scratched, cut, and abraded interfaces support inferred stiffness ranges.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Theoretical and measured dispersion curves and inferred defect measures are compared, but no scalar model-form acceptance-error map is supplied.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Stiffness ranges classify damage severity, including kappa below 1 GPa/mm approaching debonded behavior.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Linear, time-harmonic guided waves in flat isotropic laminates with small defects relative to wavelength.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Restrictions on defect shape and the quasi-static microcrack approximation are stated, but no tolerance-defined ESBC breakdown boundary is validated.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: An effective interface spring can be related to measurable defect geometry and experimentally checked in a layered structure.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not model pressure-controlled friction, stick-slip bending, contact redistribution, or continuum-versus-discrete vacuum-jamming validity.

paper_audits.title: A barrier method for frictional contact on embedded interfaces
paper_audits.physical_analogue: A stationary embedded frictional interface in a two-dimensional linear-elastic continuum.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Barrier normal-contact energy with smoothed Coulomb friction and enriched finite-element displacement jumps.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: No physical homogenized beam model; the contribution is a contact-algorithm formulation.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Barrier contact generates normal pressure, which sets Coulomb tangential capacity and affects initialization and conditioning.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: A smoothed transition between stick and slip is introduced for differentiability and Newton robustness.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Interface tractions are spatially resolved; averaged integration suppresses oscillations, but only one stationary interface is studied.
paper_audits.reference_model: Analytical inclusion benchmark, Lagrange-multiplier solutions, penalty solutions, and mesh refinement.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Contact-pressure and displacement-jump error norms and asymptotic convergence are reported, but they measure numerical accuracy.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Barrier parameters control maximum separation error and Newton convergence; no physical model-form acceptance criterion is given.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Quasi-static, infinitesimal-strain, two-dimensional linear elasticity with a single stationary embedded interface.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Early-step Newton failure and accuracy changes are numerical boundaries, not continuum homogenization breakdown.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: Normal contact, Coulomb capacity, and mixed stick-slip can be solved robustly on embedded interfaces.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not reduce many layers, compare homogenized and discrete physical models, perform experiments, or define a vacuum-jamming validity boundary.

paper_audits.title: A novel helix contact model for predicting hysteretic behavior of unbonded flexible pipes
paper_audits.physical_analogue: A multilayer unbonded flexible pipe under internal pressure and quasi-static cyclic bending.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Node-to-surface double-helix contact beams with hard normal contact and Coulomb penalty friction; the full comparator uses surface-to-surface contact.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Named equivalent layered double helix contact beam model EQUI_SHCONT2B, plus analytical plane-section and shear-interaction models.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Internal pressure and manufacturing prestress generate interlayer pressure and friction moment; assuming constant pressure in analytical models overpredicts high-pressure hysteresis.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Coulomb penalty friction with return-mapping stick-slip formulations.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Stick, transition, and slip determine stick stiffness, slip stiffness, friction moment, and dissipated energy.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: The numerical models resolve pressure distributions and ovalization; simplified analytical models assume constant pressure and thereby exhibit error.
paper_audits.reference_model: Full surface-to-surface, full-layer finite-element contact model and full-scale bending measurements.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Comparison with full-scale tests at 0.7, 10, and 20 MPa; independence from calibration is not demonstrated because friction coefficients and initial prestress are pressure-case/model calibration inputs.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Global hysteresis agreement, local penetration/deformation deviations, and 95–98% runtime reduction are reported; no uniform scalar model-form error map is provided.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Elastic slip tolerance below 10^-3 is recommended to avoid underestimating stick stiffness and friction moment.
paper_audits.declared_tolerance: The elastic-slip setting is a contact-algorithm tolerance, not a predeclared physical model-form acceptance tolerance.
paper_audits.validity_domain: One four-inch pipe under cyclic pure bending and three internal pressure levels.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Local normal-stress and transverse-slip deviations, ovalization differences, and constant-pressure analytical error are identified without a tolerance-crossing validity surface.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: A reduced contact model can reproduce pressure-dependent multilayer Coulomb hysteresis against full-layer contact and experiments while preserving key slip mechanisms.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not provide a predeclared output-specific model-form tolerance, a tolerance-defined parameter domain, or an experimentally validated breakdown boundary transferable without adapting helical-pipe mechanics.

paper_audits.title: A Single-Variable Zigzag Approach to Model Imperfect Interfaces in Layered Beams
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Two- and three-layer orthotropic beams with linear sliding-compliant interfaces under transverse loading.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Zero-thickness interfaces with no opening and linear tangential traction-displacement-jump stiffness.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Named single-variable homogenized zigzag beam theory.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Linear interfacial springs; no Coulomb capacity.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: No stick-slip transition; sliding compliance is linear.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Asymmetric interface stiffness redistributes displacement jumps and shear tractions, but normal contact is not modeled.
paper_audits.reference_model: Pagano two-dimensional exact elasticity solutions obtained through a transfer-matrix method.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Strong overlap with exact elasticity is reported for local fields, without a scalar error surface.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Response nearly reaches perfect bonding around KS h/ET=10 for two layers and 5 for three layers.
paper_audits.declared_tolerance: None; the near-overlap stiffness levels are not tolerance-defined acceptance limits.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Small-strain, simply supported, identical-material two- and three-layer beams with zero normal separation.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Known restrictions include elastic mismatch, nonlinear intralayer kinematics, finite-thickness interfaces, and other boundary conditions; no validated error boundary is supplied.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: An efficient homogenized layered-beam model can retain interface displacement jumps and reproduce exact linear imperfect-interface solutions.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not include normal pressure, Coulomb friction, finite-layer contact, experiments, or a vacuum-controlled breakdown map.

paper_audits.title: Modelling tangential friction considering contact pressure distribution of rough surfaces
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Rough flat contacts and bolted joints subjected to normal preload and cyclic tangential displacement.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Elastoplastic rough-surface finite elements generate pressure distributions that are mapped to a continuous Iwan distribution of Coulomb spring-slider elements.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Physics-based adjusted Iwan model with a twofold-Weibull slider-strength distribution and residual stiffness.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: The pressure distribution sets local normal forces, slider capacities, initial tangential stiffness, microslip-to-macroslip evolution, and energy dissipation.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Constant local Coulomb coefficient maps each normal force to a critical slip force.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Distributed Jenkins elements progressively slip from microslip to macroslip, producing stiffness softening and hysteresis.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Asperity-scale pressure statistics are resolved off-line, but the bolted-joint application assumes a uniform spatial pressure distribution and does not evolve normal contact during shear.
paper_audits.reference_model: Three-dimensional elastoplastic rough-contact finite elements, Mindlin analytical contact, classic Iwan variants, and experiments.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Published flat-contact and bolted-joint experiments across three and four preload levels; model parameters are optimized at discrete loads, so fully independent validation is not established.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Contact-pressure CDF maximum error below 0.06 and relative energy-dissipation comparisons are reported; no predeclared accept/reject map is supplied.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Microslip-to-macroslip transition and gross-slip force are physical transition measures.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Rough metal contacts under constant preload and cyclic tangential loading with fixed local friction and no dynamic separation.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Test-rig compliance and assumed uniform joint pressure cause discrepancies, but no tolerance-defined breakdown locus is validated.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: Contact-pressure distributions can be reduced to a frictional constitutive model that predicts preload-dependent stick-slip hysteresis.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not homogenize a bending stack, compare against a full multilayer contact reference over vacuum pressure, or validate a tolerance-defined breakdown boundary.

paper_audits.title: A novel friction model for steel-polymer interfaces in sliding seismic isolation bearings
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Unidirectional cyclic sliding of steel-polymer seismic-isolation interfaces.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: A lumped parallel friction law combining Coulomb, logarithmic velocity dependence, displacement-dependent breakaway, pressure modification, and thermal degradation.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Named modular five-parameter steel-polymer friction model.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: A hyperbolic-tangent factor represents reduction of friction coefficient with increasing pressure; pressure is treated as separable from velocity.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Coulomb base capacity modified by pressure, velocity, temperature, and an exponential reversal-dependent breakaway increment.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Breakaway peaks occur at direction reversal and decay exponentially with accumulated displacement; nonreversing stops do not reinitiate them for the tested interfaces.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Absent; apparent contact pressure and contact area are lumped, and true area is assumed equal to apparent area.
paper_audits.reference_model: Alternative lumped friction laws and measured force-displacement histories; no interface-resolving reference.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Specialized cyclic tests support the reversal rule, but parameter fitting and evaluation use the experimental histories; independent validation is not demonstrated.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: For oil-filled UHMWPE, R²=0.95 and maximum absolute coefficient-of-friction error=0.010 are reported after fitting.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Goodness-of-fit metrics compare friction formulations; no acceptance boundary is declared.
paper_audits.declared_tolerance: None; 0.010 is a reported fitted error, not a predeclared threshold.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Fully reversed, steady, unidirectional steel-thermoplastic sliding under the tested pressure, velocity, and thermal conditions.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Bidirectional motion, transitions to and from rest, and other materials are outside the demonstrated domain; no tolerance-crossing boundary is validated.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: A pressure-dependent steel-polymer friction law can experimentally reproduce reversal-driven breakaway and cyclic hysteresis more accurately than simpler laws.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not supply a multilayer beam continuum model, an interface-resolving reference, contact redistribution, or a predeclared validity/breakdown map.

paper_audits.title: Modeling of Stick-Slip Contact Mechanics Based on Improved Continuous-Scale Fractal-Discrete Iwan Model
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Rough steel interfaces under combined normal loading and cyclic tangential displacement.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Continuous-scale fractal asperity contact coupled to discrete Jenkins/Iwan spring-slider elements.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Normal force controls real contact, normal stiffness, slider-force distribution, gross-slip displacement, and saturation force.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Uniform macroscopic Coulomb coefficient assigns slip capacities to Jenkins units.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Progressive microslip softens stiffness, followed by macroslip with constant residual stiffness.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Normal force is statistically distributed among asperities, but mutual asperity interaction and evolving surface morphology are neglected.
paper_audits.reference_model: Earlier fractal contact models and literature steel-contact experiments; no full structural interface-resolving reference.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Comparison with secondary experimental hysteresis loops at approximately 200–600 N.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Close curve agreement is stated, but no general scalar model-form error surface or declared acceptance tolerance is supported.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Critical macroslip displacement and saturation force mark a physical transition.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Unidirectional rough steel contact with fixed topology, uniform friction, simplified elastic/plastic asperity states, and no wear.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Model assumptions fail for interacting asperities, evolving wear, localized friction variation, or soft viscoelastic materials; no validated threshold is supplied.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: Normal load and roughness can be linked to distributed stick-slip response and macroslip onset.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not establish multilayer bending homogenization error, vacuum actuation transfer, or a tolerance-defined continuum breakdown boundary.

paper_audits.title: Fretting wear modeling of bolted joint interface with microscopic roughness using the 1D microslip friction model and equivalent thin layer
paper_audits.physical_analogue: A preloaded bolted lap-joint interface represented along its contact length and subjected to cyclic fretting.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Nonuniform exponent-law pressure, Coulomb shear capacity, Greenwood-Williamson microcontact compliance, and Archard wear.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: One-dimensional continuum elastic-beam microslip model with an equivalent thin interfacial layer.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Preload sets a nonuniform pressure field and Coulomb capacity; cyclic wear reduces pressure in the slip region while the stuck region retains initial pressure.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Constant-coefficient Coulomb friction combined with pressure- and roughness-dependent tangential stiffness.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: The model predicts stuck length, slip length, microslip initiation, full slip, hysteresis, and wear localized to the slip region.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Pressure redistribution evolves through wear-induced separation in the microslip region.
paper_audits.reference_model: Published joint hysteresis data and direct plane-contact wear tests; no explicit three-dimensional interface-resolving model-form reference is supplied.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Published hysteresis experiments and new 60–120 N fretting-wear tests are used, but validation targets differ and independent validation of the entire reduced model is not established.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Average relative wear-depth error of 13.54% and hysteresis displacement/energy comparisons are reported.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Minimum force for microslip and maximum force for full slip are physical thresholds.
paper_audits.declared_tolerance: None; 13.54% is a reported prediction error.
paper_audits.validity_domain: One-dimensional metal lap contact with elastic GW asperities, constant friction, prescribed pressure shape, and cyclic fretting.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: No tolerance-defined reduced-versus-full breakdown boundary; elastoplastic asperities, debris, and multidirectional behavior are excluded.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: A reduced continuum/equivalent-layer model can connect nonuniform preload, Coulomb capacity, stick-slip extent, evolving pressure, and experimentally measured wear or hysteresis.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not provide a multilayer bending discrete reference, predeclared model-form tolerance, or experimentally validated vacuum-pressure breakdown boundary.

paper_audits.title: Theoretical, experimental, and numerical simulation studies on interface slip in steel-concrete composite continuous beams with high-strength bolted connectors
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Steel-concrete composite beams connected by preloaded high-strength bolts under static bending.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Uniformly distributed linear-elastic bolt shear stiffness relating interface shear to slip.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Analytical second-order interface-slip equation and slip-induced deflection correction.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Bolt preload is specified, but it does not explicitly drive a Coulomb stick-slip capacity in the analytical law.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: The evidence describes linear connector stiffness rather than a pressure-dependent Coulomb friction law.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Continuous elastic slip is predicted; stick, partial slip, and gross slip are not resolved.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: No evolving normal-contact redistribution in the analytical model.
paper_audits.reference_model: Three-dimensional Abaqus model with bolts, concrete damage, and steel plasticity.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: One inverted simply supported beam test validates overall structural behavior; analytical service-stage slip comparisons are principally against FEA.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Peak slip differences of 2.03–2.09% and deflection errors of 0.773–2.714% versus FEA are reported; ignoring slip gives much larger errors.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: No predeclared acceptance criterion; reported percentages compare analytical and numerical outputs.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Elastic service-stage steel-concrete composite response with uniformly distributed linear bolt connectors.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Cracking, yielding, and failure stages are observed physically, but they are not linked to failure of the reduced model under a declared tolerance.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: A reduced slip-inclusive beam equation can substantially improve deflection and slip predictions against a detailed model.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not supply pressure-dependent Coulomb slip evolution, a multilayer frictional reference, or a tolerance-defined applicability map.

paper_audits.title: A novel frictional contact correction transfer matrix method for bolted vibration systems: modeling, simulation, and experimental validation
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Preloaded bolted beam-like assemblies under piezoelectrically excited vibration.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: An equivalent angular frictional-contact correction represents interface compliance and lifting; tangential microslip is omitted.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Named Frictional Contact Correction Transfer Matrix Method.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Torque is calibrated to preload and a first-slip friction coefficient is measured, but detailed pressure-dependent tangential mechanics are not included in the reduced state equations.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Static frictional contact is represented through a correction coefficient rather than explicit evolving Coulomb partial slip.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Local tangential microslip and partial slip are explicitly neglected.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Interface separation/compliance is represented in aggregate; spatial pressure redistribution is not resolved.
paper_audits.reference_model: Frictional-contact finite elements, bonded finite elements, other transfer-matrix variants, and modal experiments.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Three physical assemblies are tested with scanning laser vibrometry; friction and torque-preload are separately characterized.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: First-mode errors of about 1.27–3.07% and second-mode errors up to -13.21% are reported, with speedups of 117–601 times.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: A 3% finite-element mesh-sensitivity criterion and iterative convergence tolerances are used; higher-mode overcorrection is observed.
paper_audits.declared_tolerance: The 3% and iteration tolerances govern numerical convergence, not physical model-form acceptance.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Small-motion bending-dominated vibration of the three tested bolted configurations, chiefly the first mode.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Second-mode overcorrection demonstrates output-dependent deterioration, but no predeclared tolerance boundary over preload or contact state is constructed.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: A low-order contact-correction model can match first-mode experiments and contact FEM while failing more strongly in another mode.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not model multilayer Coulomb stick-slip, quasi-static planar bending, vacuum-pressure coupling, or a tolerance-defined breakdown map.

paper_audits.title: Stick-slip friction model for soft-hard joints under preload degradation
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Precompressed soft-hard damping interfaces under cyclic tangential shear with viscoelastic preload decay.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Uniform parallel-plate contact with a physics-informed algebraic hysteretic law and a differential Jenkins/Iwan comparator.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Closed-form algebraic stick-slip friction model for harmonic loading.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Normal pressure enters the dynamic friction scaling and evolves through viscoelastic relaxation; hysteresis evolution is predicted without recalibration.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Pressure-, velocity-, roughness-, adhesion-, and viscoelasticity-dependent friction with power-law slip-area evolution and Masing-type cyclic mapping.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Local microslip grows to global macroslip at a critical displacement, with stiffness softening and later friction-induced stiffening.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: A uniform nominal pressure is used; spatial redistribution among multiple layers is absent.
paper_audits.reference_model: A 15-element differential Jenkins/Iwan model and experimental rubber/granite and silicone-foam/steel data.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Published steady sliding data and cyclic foam experiments across pressure, velocity, and frequency; some reduced parameters remain empirically fitted.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: Algebraic-versus-differential amplitude error is below 0.5%; experimental loop-area error is within 3.3%.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: Critical displacement defines macroslip; reported 0.5% and 3.3% errors quantify performance but are not declared acceptance limits.
paper_audits.declared_tolerance: None demonstrated as a predeclared model-form acceptance tolerance.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Soft-hard, one-dimensional tangential contact under steady sliding or symmetric harmonic loading with constant or slowly degrading compression.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: General loading, strong adhesion-edge effects, high-speed thermal damage, wear, and multiaxial contact require additional mechanics; no tolerance-defined failure boundary is validated.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: A compact reduced friction model can couple preload degradation to micro-to-macro slip and reproduce soft-interface hysteresis experimentally.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not model a bending multilayer stack, compare continuum and full-layer contact models, or validate a vacuum-pressure-dependent breakdown boundary.

paper_audits.title: The global-local mechanical behaviors of multilayered structure and applications to superconducting coils
paper_audits.physical_analogue: Large stacks of dry contacting plates and wound superconducting tapes under bending or electromagnetic loading.
paper_audits.interface_or_connection_model: Negligible-gap adjacent-shell contact with Coulomb friction formulated as an internal yield condition and homogenized into continuum shear/internal forces.
paper_audits.reduced_or_equivalent_model: Named continuum theory for multilayered structures with continuous through-stack interpolation, modified strain kinematics, and homogenized contact/friction.
paper_audits.normal_contact_pressure_role: Local normal contact stress enters Coulomb capacity through the yield condition; applied loading generates the contact field, but vacuum pressure is not separately modeled or swept.
paper_audits.friction_law_or_capacity: Coulomb yield function with maximum dissipation and associative-flow-style update.
paper_audits.stick_slip_mechanism: Stick and slip produce path-dependent frictional dissipation and stiffness enhancement; explicit gross-slip boundary mapping is not reported.
paper_audits.contact_redistribution: Normal stress and homogenized friction are fields in the continuum and discrete reference, but separation is prohibited by the negligible-gap assumption.
paper_audits.reference_model: Penalty-based discrete contact model with individual layers, supplemented by multilayer bending and coil experiments.
paper_audits.experimental_validation: Force-displacement response for 35-, 50-, and 70-layer plate stacks and hoop strain for a five-turn coil are reproduced; experiments support response predictions but do not sample both sides of the derived 5% breakdown boundary.
paper_audits.quantitative_error_evidence: For 30 layers at 27 degrees, out-of-plane and in-plane displacement errors are about 3% and 6%. A 5% maximum-displacement threshold gives permissible rotations of about 20 degrees for 30 layers and 7.5 degrees for 150 layers.
paper_audits.criterion_or_threshold: A 5% maximum displacement-error threshold against the discrete contact model defines layer-count-dependent permissible rotation limits.
paper_audits.declared_tolerance: 5% maximum displacement error relative to the discrete contact model.
paper_audits.validity_domain: Quasi-static axisymmetric or two-dimensional multilayer deformation with negligible gaps, moderate rotations, and friction not dominant enough to violate Kirchhoff-Love kinematics; the mapped rotation limit decreases with layer count.
paper_audits.breakdown_boundary: Numerically established 5% error-crossing boundaries include about 20 degrees at n=30 and 7.5 degrees at n=150. The supplied experiments validate responses within selected cases but do not experimentally validate the boundary crossing itself.
paper_audits.what_it_proves: Frictional multilayer homogenization can be compared quantitatively with discrete contact, classified by an explicit error tolerance, swept over layer count and deformation, and checked against multilayer bending experiments.
paper_audits.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not show that vacuum-generated and spatially evolving normal contact satisfies the zero-gap assumptions, sweep vacuum pressure, independently validate the tolerance-crossing breakdown boundary, or cover regimes where friction becomes dominant or layers separate.

high_threat_criterion_audit.criterion: Pressure, prestress, friction-coefficient, element, and contact sensitivities are compared while reproducing full-scale pipe hysteresis.
high_threat_criterion_audit.assessment: This is a strong pressure-contact-friction analogue and full-layer experimental benchmark, but it does not define reduced-model acceptance or breakdown.

high_threat_criterion_audit.source: Wang, Ye, and Yue (2022), paper_id a300a3b714
high_threat_criterion_audit.criterion: Elastic slip tolerance below 10^-3 is needed to avoid underpredicting stick stiffness and friction moment.
high_threat_criterion_audit.assessment: The threshold controls penalty-friction numerical behavior. It cannot be counted as a physical reduced-model acceptance tolerance.

high_threat_criterion_audit.criterion: Microslip-to-macroslip transition and gross-slip capacity emerge from pressure-distributed Jenkins elements.
high_threat_criterion_audit.assessment: It supplies pressure-to-capacity-to-slip mechanics and experiments, but a physical slip transition is not a continuum-model breakdown boundary.

high_threat_criterion_audit.criterion: Maximum absolute coefficient-of-friction error of 0.010 and R²=0.95 are reported for the fitted model.
high_threat_criterion_audit.assessment: The values quantify fitted predictive performance but are not predeclared acceptance thresholds and do not delimit a continuum validity domain.

high_threat_criterion_audit.criterion: Minimum tangential load for microslip and maximum load for full slip partition the physical contact state.
high_threat_criterion_audit.assessment: The equivalent-thin-layer model closely matches the pressure-friction-slip chain, including pressure redistribution through wear, but the thresholds govern slip state rather than reduced-model validity.

high_threat_criterion_audit.criterion: A 3% finite-element mesh-sensitivity target and formulation-specific iterative convergence tolerances are used.
high_threat_criterion_audit.assessment: These are numerical controls. The observed -13.21% second-mode error is a reported failure, not a predeclared tolerance boundary.

high_threat_criterion_audit.criterion: Critical lateral displacement marks macro-slip; reduced-versus-differential error below 0.5% and experimental loop-area error within 3.3% are reported.
high_threat_criterion_audit.assessment: This strongly threatens any claim based only on preload-dependent soft-interface stick-slip or reduced hysteresis modeling, but neither percentage is established as an acceptance threshold or mapped breakdown boundary.

high_threat_criterion_audit.criterion: A 5% maximum displacement-error threshold against a discrete contact model yields permissible rotations of about 20 degrees for 30 layers and 7.5 degrees for 150 layers.
high_threat_criterion_audit.assessment: This is C03's closest kill evidence. It supplies an explicit tolerance-based continuum-versus-discrete validity boundary for frictional multilayers and separately compares the model with experiments. The boundary itself is not experimentally validated, vacuum pressure is not swept, separation is prohibited, and large-friction regimes are excluded.

kill_test.evidence_summary: Collectively, C03 establishes named reduced models, full-layer/discrete-contact references, pressure and friction parameters, quantitative model-form errors, and finite sweeps. Most importantly, ca46dc062d uses an explicit 5% displacement-error threshold to define layer-count-dependent rotation limits for a frictional multilayer continuum against a discrete contact model. Flexible-pipe and joint-contact papers separately establish pressure-dependent Coulomb capacity, stick-transition-slip evolution, contact redistribution, reduced representations, and experimental comparison. The chain still fails at items 8 and 9. The 5% continuum breakdown boundary is numerical rather than experimentally validated at tolerance crossing, while experiments demonstrate selected responses rather than the boundary. Direct transfer to vacuum layer jamming is also not established: ca46dc062d enforces negligible gaps, does not sweep vacuum pressure, and excludes friction-dominant regimes; flexible-pipe pressure/contact models use helical geometry, calibrated residual prestress, and no declared error boundary. Combining these families would require new vacuum-to-contact-field modeling and validation rather than a demonstrated transfer.

strongest_threats.why_it_matters: It already combines frictional multilayer homogenization, a discrete-contact reference, layer-count and rotation sweeps, quantitative errors, an explicit 5% applicability threshold, a validity boundary, and multilayer bending experiments.
strongest_threats.remaining_gap: The tolerance-crossing boundary is not experimentally validated; vacuum pressure is not an input sweep; zero gap is assumed; and large-friction or separation regimes require different mechanics.

strongest_threats.source: Wang, Ye, and Yue (2022), paper_id a300a3b714
strongest_threats.why_it_matters: It links pressure and initial contact stress to Coulomb stick-transition-slip bending, compares a named reduced helix-contact model with a full-layer surface-contact model, and uses full-scale experiments.
strongest_threats.remaining_gap: No predeclared physical error tolerance or tolerance-defined breakdown surface is provided, and transfer from helical pipe contact to flat vacuum-clamped sheets is not demonstrated.

strongest_threats.why_it_matters: It provides a full-layer, pressure-dependent Coulomb-contact reference with experimentally observed quasi-static bending hysteresis across three pressure levels.
strongest_threats.remaining_gap: It is primarily a reference model rather than a reduced-versus-full validity framework; initial stress and friction inputs are calibrated, and no declared breakdown criterion exists.

strongest_threats.why_it_matters: It experimentally connects preload and preload degradation to a compact stick-slip model, micro-to-macro slip evolution, and quantitative hysteresis errors in a soft-hard interface.
strongest_threats.remaining_gap: It is a dynamic/harmonic single-interface law with uniform pressure, not a multilayer beam homogenization study, and its errors are not acceptance thresholds.

strongest_threats.why_it_matters: It maps a resolved contact-pressure distribution into a reduced Iwan constitutive law and validates preload-dependent hysteresis and microslip-to-macroslip behavior experimentally.
strongest_threats.remaining_gap: Normal-contact redistribution during structural bending is not retained, no multilayer discrete reference is used, and no tolerance-defined validity domain is supplied.

strongest_threats.why_it_matters: It combines an equivalent thin layer, a continuum beam, nonuniform preload, Coulomb microslip, evolving pressure redistribution, experiments, and quantitative prediction error.
strongest_threats.remaining_gap: The target is fretting wear in a single bolted interface; no full multilayer bending reference or predeclared model-form breakdown criterion is provided.

strongest_threats.why_it_matters: It experimentally supports a pressure-dependent steel-polymer friction law with explicit displacement-history-driven breakaway and quantitative error measures.
strongest_threats.remaining_gap: It is a calibrated lumped friction law without a multilayer continuum, discrete contact reference, contact redistribution, or tolerance-defined breakdown boundary.

surviving_gap: The generic method has largely been occupied: frictional multilayer continuum theories, discrete-contact comparators, layer-count sweeps, quantitative output error, and even a declared 5% applicability boundary already exist. P1 survives only if it demonstrates a vacuum-specific failure mechanism or transfer limit that these frameworks do not already resolve. The required contribution is an independently validated, output-specific tolerance boundary showing how vacuum pressure generates and redistributes normal contact across many flat layers and how that field changes Coulomb capacity and stick/partial-slip/gross-slip during quasi-static planar bending. The boundary must test assumptions already exposed as fragile in the corpus—negligible gap, prescribed or constant pressure, friction remaining nondominant, and calibration of contact parameters—and experiments must sample accepted and rejected sides of the boundary rather than merely agree with the model at selected conditions.
c04_search_rationale: A narrow C04 is justified by two specific unresolved threats, not by a generic demand for more literature. First, DOI 10.1061/JSENDH.STENG-13096 remains unavailable despite being previously identified as high threat and must be obtained and audited. Second, ca46dc062d reveals a precise forward-citation family to test: frictional multilayer continuum-versus-discrete studies that experimentally validate an explicit tolerance-crossing boundary while varying externally imposed normal pressure or preload and permitting contact opening/redistribution. Search should be limited to that family and forward citations of ca46dc062d and the flexible-pipe reduced-contact work.
recommended_next_action: Run a tightly scoped C04 retrieval and forward-citation audit for DOI 10.1061/JSENDH.STENG-13096 and for successors to ca46dc062d that combine pressure/preload sweeps, frictional multilayer homogenization, discrete contact, declared error tolerance, and experimental validation of the boundary. In parallel, preregister P1's exact reduced model, full-layer reference, calibration/validation split, outputs, tolerances, and test points on both sides of the predicted boundary; explicitly include vacuum-to-contact-pressure mapping, possible layer separation, and pressure redistribution.
